take: Takomo launched in 2021 out of Turku, Finland with a premise that shouldn't be radical but somehow still is: forged irons, clean design, half the price. No pro shop markup, no retail middlemen, no tour-van mythology. They design the clubs, partner with top-tier foundries, and ship direct. The savings go straight to the price tag — a full set of S20C forged cavity backs for $649, when comparable Japanese-forged sets from Mizuno or Srixon run well north of a thousand.
story_extra: The lineup spans every skill level. The 101 MKII is a hollow-body game-improvement iron that won MyGolfSpy's Best GI Iron — serious forgiveness at $579 for a seven-piece set. The 201T MKII, new for 2026, is a players precision iron aimed at better ball strikers who want workability without giving up distance. And the 301 CB is the crown jewel: single-billet S20C carbon steel, forged and finished with the kind of feel you associate with boutique Japanese smithing, not a DTC brand that also sells $15 gloves. Wesley Bryan played Takomo irons on the PGA Tour. The Skyforger wedge, at $99, uses the same 8620 steel alloy that Cleveland and Vokey charge nearly double for.

The Scandinavian design DNA shows up everywhere — minimal branding, matte finishes, clean toplines. No loud graphics, no oversized cavities screaming for attention. Takomo makes the case that the traditional equipment pricing model is broken, and then they prove it by shipping clubs that perform alongside irons three times their price. If you haven't heard of them yet, you will.

related.why: Two ex-Nike craftsmen in Nike's old Fort Worth building — wedges ground by hand, fitting required.
David Edel fitted putters by where you actually aim, measured with a mirror and a laser. He sold the company in 2023; the method outlived him.
Terry Koehler's wedge company on the Gulf Coast — the patented Koehler Sole, built to order.
